advances: Strict raw local gain in a positive nonvertex fiber over its attained ordinary maximum. The gain uses selected compatible sources and is independent of the total mass in unselected fibers.

proof:
Since $E\subseteq K_w$, one has $r,\rho\le R$ and $\|v\|\le2R$ for $v=m-g$. A nonvertical through-mark cap can be normalized to continuous unit normal $u$ and base tilt $a$. At the old mark $(w,g)$ its margin at $(p,x)$ is $a\cdot(p-w)+u\cdot(x-g)$. Let $b_i$ be its maximum over $K_{p_i}$. The base moment condition cancels the common tilt, giving
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i b_i=h_E(u)-u\cdot g\ge u\cdot v+\rho,
$$
where $h_E$ is the support function of $E$.

If $u\cdot v\ge-\rho/2$, some $b_i\ge\rho/2$. About a point attaining $b_i$, the homothetic copy of $K_{p_i}$ of ratio $\rho/(4R)$ stays in that old cap, since every directional width is at most $2R$. It supplies volume at least $\Delta$, in addition to own cap volume at least $A$. Every section of each selected fiber perpendicular to $u$ has area at most $\omega R^{d-1}$, including the counting-section convention for $d=1$. Integrating over a threshold displacement therefore bounds the selected mass loss when moving the mark by $L\varepsilon\|v\|\le\Delta/2$. The new cap has mass at least $A+\Delta/2$.

If $u\cdot v<-\rho/2$, the move lowers the threshold by $-\varepsilon u\cdot v>\varepsilon\rho/2$, at most $r/2$. All traces grow. The newly included slab of the own ball has section areas at least $\omega(r/2)^{d-1}$ and therefore adds at least $\omega(r/2)^{d-1}\varepsilon\rho/2$ to $A$. A pure base containing halfspace includes the whole own fiber. Opposite ordinary caps at $g$ partition its volume up to a null hyperplane, so $A\le |K_w|/2$. Also $G\le\Delta/2\le |K_w|/2$. This proves the same lower bound for pure base caps, and any containing cap contains its parallel through-mark cap. Since $1-\varepsilon>0$, the segment from $g$ to $m$ gives an interior point at $y$.

To choose the inballs quantitatively, use 6769574fc1bd9f8d on each selected body with selector mass equal to that body's full volume. Its metronoid is the centroid, so every centroid cap has mass at least $\Gamma_d\nu$. This bound also holds at the own deepest point $g$. In direction $u$, the cap at any such point has volume at most $\omega R^{d-1}$ times its thickness to the supporting plane, by the same section bound. Thus the thickness is at least $\Gamma_d\nu/(\omega R^{d-1})$ in every direction. The support halfspaces give the corresponding inballs about the centroids and $g$, and Minkowski addition gives the ball of that radius about $m$ in $E$.

For an actual nonvertex positive base, Carathéodory applied to the other positive bases gives such a representation with $k\le n+1$, and convexity of the source gives the required Minkowski inclusion. The chosen Minkowski sum is full dimensional. An ordinary deepest point exists in the interior: ordinary through-cap mass is jointly continuous in the mark and unit normal by nullity of hyperplanes, and minimization over the compact sphere preserves continuity. An interior ball gives positive depth while supporting caps at boundary points have zero volume. Compactness then yields an interior maximizer. The constructed interior mark has raw mixed depth at least $A+G$ even with all original fibers retained. The mixed depth on a compact own fiber attains a maximum: for each fixed ambient normal the finite measure of the closed through-mark cap is upper semicontinuous by continuity from above, and taking the infimum preserves upper semicontinuity. Zero-volume fibers add no mass. Replacing $k+1$ by $n+2$ in $L$ preserves the upper bound on threshold losses and can only weaken the gain.
statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let distinct real bases $p_1,\ldots,p_k$, all different from $w$, have weights $\lambda_i>0$ of sum one with $\sum_i\lambda_ip_i=w$. Suppose the full-dimensional compact convex fibers satisfy $E=\sum_i\lambda_iK_{p_i}\subseteq K_w$. Let $g$ be an ordinary deepest point of $K_w$ with raw depth $A$, and assume $B(g,r)\subseteq K_w$ and $B(m,\rho)\subseteq E$ for $r,\rho>0$. Each selected fiber lies in some radius-$R$ Euclidean ball, with centers allowed to differ. Let $\nu>0$ be the least selected volume, and let $\omega$ be the $(d-1)$-dimensional unit ball volume, with $\omega=1$ for $d=1$. Define
$$
L=(k+1)\omega R^{d-1},\qquad \Delta=\nu(\rho/(4R))^d,\qquad
\varepsilon=\min\{1/2,r/(4R),\Delta/(4RL)\},\qquad
G=\min\{\Delta/2,\omega(r/2)^{d-1}\varepsilon\rho/2\}.
$$
The point $y=g+\varepsilon(m-g)$ is interior to $K_w$, and every closed ambient halfspace containing $(w,y)$ has summed selected fiber volume at least $A+G$. Additional positive measure can only increase the bound. One may take $r=\rho=\Gamma_d\nu/(\omega R^{d-1})$, where $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and $m=\sum_i\lambda_i g_i$ with $g_i$ the centroid of $K_{p_i}$.

In particular, for the positive integer fibers of a compact convex set, at every nonvertex positive base $w$ of their convex hull the attained maximal raw mixed depth on $K_w$ strictly exceeds the attained maximal raw ordinary depth $A$ of $K_w$, and hence exceeds $\Gamma_d|K_w|$. One can choose $k\le n+1$ for bases in $\mathbb R^n$.
title: Explicit strict mixed-depth gain at a nonvertex fiber
